title: Atlassian: No Denying Now That AI Is A Tailwind
text: Atlassian has rebounded sharply, with AI driving demand tailwinds and the stock up ~10% YTD after a strong fiscal Q4. TEAM's core bull case rests on a massive $67B SAM, low market penetration, and Jira's leadership in developer workflow collaboration. Rovo AI assistant usage surged 50% QoQ, with credits-based, usage-driven pricing unlocking new consumption revenue streams beyond seat-based models.

title: Brookfield Corporation: Buybacks, Corporate Simplification, And Record AUM (Rating Downgrade)
text: Brookfield Corporation is rated Buy, driven by record fee-bearing capital and assets under management growth during the second quarter. BN's ongoing corporate simplification will enhance share accessibility and trading liquidity and broaden its shareholder base by year-end 2026. Distributable earnings per share rose 15% year-over-year, supporting $580 million in share buybacks, though the dividend yield remains modest at 0.67%.

title: Ameresco: A $1.5 Billion AI Power Backlog Changes The Story
text: Ameresco is rated Buy, with upside potential driven by a $1.5 billion awarded data center backlog—significantly larger than its $2 billion annual revenue base. AMRC's valuation trades at a discount to historical averages, reflecting market skepticism about converting awarded backlog into contracted revenue. Leverage is high at ~$1.82 billion in net debt (~7.5x EBITDA), but much is project-backed; cash flow remains negative, and interest expense is substantial.

title: Corpay's Corporate Payments Push Could Unlock Its Next Growth Phase
text: Corpay is rated BUY after strong 2Q26 results and raised full-year guidance, with robust earnings and revenue growth. CPAY is shifting focus from vehicle to corporate payments, targeting a $560 billion TAM with less than 1% current share. 2Q26 revenue rose 21% to $1.34B, adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 57.3%, and free cash flow hit $1.6B TTM.

title: Siemens Healthineers: Successful Investment, Updating For H2 2026
text: Siemens Healthineers remains a high-conviction BUY with a reiterated €48/share price target, reflecting strong Imaging and Precision Therapy segments. I exclude Chinese recovery from my base case; growth is now driven by ex-China Imaging and Varian, with diagnostics seen as structurally impaired. 3Q26 results confirmed robust order momentum (1.3x book-to-bill), and margin strength (19.1%), and EPS guidance raised to €2.45, though tariff refunds contributed.

title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise: AI Infrastructure And Juniper Could Unlock The Next Growth Phase
text: Hewlett Packard Enterprise earns a buy rating, driven by surging AI infrastructure demand and a strengthened networking business post-Juniper acquisition. HPE posted record Q2 FY2026 revenue of $10.7 billion (+40% YoY), with Cloud and AI revenue up 22.9% and Networking revenue up 148.2%. Profitability is improving: Q2 non-GAAP EPS grew 108% YoY, Cloud and AI operating margin nearly doubled, and free cash flow guidance was raised to at least $3.5 billion.

Revenue and profitability have accelerated, with Q1 2027 revenue up 36.2% and broad-based volume gains across core categories. SENEA's recent acquisitions, notably Green Giant's US frozen business, are fueling expansion beyond organic growth.

title: Safe Pro Group: AI Takes Off, But A High-Risk Buy
text: Safe Pro Group receives a high-risk buy rating with a $7.16 price target, reflecting roughly 33% upside potential. SPAI's AI segment now leads revenue growth, posting 1,336% YoY Q2 revenue growth and securing over $5 million in 2026 AI-related orders. Gross margin expanded to 64%, but customer concentration, lack of SaaS revenue, and continued operating losses highlight ongoing risks.

title: Teleflex: Portfolio Surgery Creates A Better Medtech Compounder
text: Teleflex is transforming into a focused procedural technology platform, divesting lower-growth units and reinvesting in high-acuity Vascular and Surgical segments. TFX's Vascular and Surgical segments are generating high-single-digit growth, while Interventional segment weakness is attributed to temporary integration challenges. Proceeds from divestitures are funding debt reduction and substantial share repurchases, enhancing per-share earnings potential and financial flexibility.
